title: 断五下分结之道行
note: 断五下分结：欲贪、嗔等根除

evidence.pali: ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. So yadeva tattha hoti vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ…pe… anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 复次，阿难，比丘遍超一切色想，灭有对想，不作意种种想，思惟‘虚空无边’，具足空无边处而住。彼于其处，凡所有受、想、行、识……从彼世间，为不还法。阿难，此亦是道，此亦是行道，为断五下分结。
evidence.english: “Furthermore, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, with the complete transcending of perceptions of form, with the cessation of perceptions of resistance, and by not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ enters and dwells in the base of the infinity of space. He regards whatever phenomena there that pertain to feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness… he is of the nature of not returning from that world. This too, Ānanda, is indeed the path, this is the practice for the abandoning of the five lower fetters.”

entries.pali: 35 . Anāgāminiddese – orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanāna nti oraṃ vuccati kāmadhātu. Yassa imāni pañca bandhanāni appahīnāni honti, so bhavagge nibbattopi gilitabaḷiso maccho viya dīghasuttakena pāde baddhakāko viya tehi bandhanehi ākaḍḍhiyamāno kāmadhātuyaṃyeva pavattatīti pañca bandhanāni orambhāgiyānī ti vuccanti. Heṭṭhābhāgiyāni heṭṭhākoṭṭhāsikānīti attho. Parikkhayā ti tesaṃ bandhanānaṃ parikkhayena. Opapātiko ti upapātayoniko. Imināssa gabbhaseyyā paṭikkhittā. Tattha parinibbāyī ti tattha suddhāvāsaloke parinibbāyitā. Anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā ti paṭisandhiggahaṇavasena tasmā lokā idha anāvattanasabhāvo. Buddhadassanatheradassanadhammassavanānaṃ panatthāyassa āgamanaṃ anivāritaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccatī ti ayaṃ evaṃvidho puggalo paṭisandhivasena puna anāgamanato anāgāmī nāma vuccati.
entries.chinese_simplified: 35. 不还者（anāgāmī）的解释——下分结（orambhāgiya saṃyojana）：‘下’（oraṃ）指欲界（kāmadhātu）。若人未断此五种束缚（bandhana），则纵使生于有顶天（bhavagga），亦如吞钩之鱼被长绳所牵，如足系绳索之乌鸦，被此等束缚牵引而流转于欲界，故此五种束缚名为五下分结。下分（heṭṭhābhāgiya）即下部分之义。断尽（parikkhaya）：即断尽此等束缚。化生者（opapātika）：即由化生（upapātayoni）而生者，以此排除胎生（gabbhaseyyā）。于彼处般涅槃（tattha parinibbāyī）：即于彼净居天（suddhāvāsa）般涅槃。不还法，从彼世间（anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā）：指依结生而言，有从彼世间不复还来此间之性。然为见佛、见长老、闻法故，其来此则无障碍。此谓：如是之人（puggala），因由结生不复还来，故名为不还者。
entries.english: 35. In the explanation of the Non-Returner: Regarding 'the lower fetters,' 'ora' is said to be the sense-sphere realm. For one who has not abandoned these five bonds, even if reborn in the highest existence, he is dragged back by those bonds—like a fish that has swallowed a baited hook or a crow with its foot tied by a long string—and continues in the sense-sphere realm. Thus, these five bonds are called 'the lower fetters.' This means they belong to the lower part, that is, they are of the lower portion. 'By the destruction' means by the destruction of those bonds. 'Spontaneously born' means born of spontaneous birth; by this, womb-birth is rejected for him. 'Attains final Nibbāna there' means he is one who attains final Nibbāna in that Pure Abode world. 'One whose nature is not to return from that world' means his nature is not to return here from that world by way of taking rebirth. However, his coming for the sake of seeing the Buddha, the elders, or hearing the Dhamma is not prevented. 'This is called' means this kind of person, on account of not coming again by way of rebirth, is called a 'Non-Returner'.

entries.pali: Tanuttā ti pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya ca kadāci karahaci uppattiyā ca tanubhāvā. Orambhāgiyāna nti heṭṭhābhāgiyānaṃ, ye hi baddho upari suddhāvāsabhūmiyaṃ nibbattituṃ na sakkoti. Opapātiko ti sesayonipaṭikkhepavacanametaṃ. Tattha parinibbāyī ti tasmiṃ uparibhaveyeva parinibbānadhammo. Anāvattidhammo ti tato brahmalokā puna paṭisandhivasena anāvattanadhammo. Cetovimutti nti cittavisuddhiṃ, sabbakilesabandhanavimuttassa arahattaphalacittassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Paññāvimutti nti etthāpi sabbakilesabandhanavimuttā arahattaphalapaññāva paññāvimuttīti veditabbā. Diṭṭheva dhamme ti imasmiṃyeva attabhāve. Saya nti sāmaṃ. Abhiññā ti abhijānitvā. Sacchikatvā ti paccakkhaṃ katvā. Atha vā abhiññā sacchikatvā ti abhiññāya abhivisiṭṭhena ñāṇena sacchikaritvātipi attho. Upasampajjā ti patvā paṭilabhitvā. Idaṃ sutvā licchavirājā cintesi – ‘‘ayaṃ pana dhammo na sakuṇena viya uppatitvā, nāpi godhāya viya urena gantvā sakkā paṭivijjhituṃ , addhā pana imaṃ paṭivijjhantassa pubbabhāgappaṭipadāya bhavitabbaṃ, pucchāmi tāva na’’nti.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘薄’（tanuttā），是由于现行微弱，时而、偶尔才生起，状态稀薄之故。‘下分结’（orambhāgiyāni），即属于下界的结；被它们所束缚者，无法投生到上面的净居天（suddhāvāsa）。‘化生’（opapātika），此词排除了其他投生方式。‘于彼处般涅槃’（tattha parinibbāyī），即在那上界有中就有般涅槃的本性。‘不还法’（anāvattidhamma）者，即有不再从彼梵天界以结生方式返回的本性者。‘心解脱’（cetovimutti），即心的清净，这是对已从一切烦恼束缚中解脱的阿罗汉果心的称谓。‘慧解脱’（paññāvimutti），于此也应了知，从一切烦恼束缚中解脱的阿罗汉果慧，即是慧解脱。‘于现法中’（diṭṭheva dhamme），即在这一生中。‘自’（sayaṃ），即亲自。‘以证知’（abhiññā），即直接了知之后。‘作证后’（sacchikatvā），即亲身证实之后。或者，‘以证知作证’（abhiññā sacchikatvā）的意思也可以是：以证知，即以殊胜的智慧作证之后。‘证得’（upasampajja），即达到、获得之后。离车王（Licchavirājā）听后心想：‘此法并非像鸟一样飞起，或像蜥蜴一样用胸膛爬行就能通达。诚然，要通达此法，必须有前分道。我且先就此请教。’
entries.english: “Attenuation” (tanuttā) is due to the weakness of their manifestation and their arising only occasionally, thus their attenuated state. “Of those pertaining to the lower part” (orambhāgiyānaṃ) means: of those pertaining to the lower part. For one bound by these is unable to be reborn above in the Pure Abodes. “Spontaneously arisen” (opapātiko) is a term that excludes the remaining modes of birth. “Attaining final Nibbāna there” (tattha parinibbāyī) means: one who is of the nature to attain final Nibbāna in that very higher existence. “Of a nature not to return” (anāvattidhammo) means: one who is of the nature not to return from that brahma world by way of rebirth-linking. “Liberation of mind” (cetovimuttiṃ) means: the purity of mind. This is a designation for the mind of the fruit of arahantship, which is liberated from all bonds of defilements. Here too, “liberation by wisdom” (paññāvimuttiṃ) should be understood as the wisdom of the fruit of arahantship, which is liberated from all bonds of defilements. “In this very life” (diṭṭheva dhamme) means: in this very existence. “By oneself” (sayaṃ) means: on one’s own. “Through direct knowledge” (abhiññā) means: having known through higher knowledge. “Having realized” (sacchikatvā) means: having made it manifest. Alternatively, “having realized through direct knowledge” (abhiññā sacchikatvā) also means: having realized through direct knowledge, that is, through superior knowledge. “Having entered upon” (upasampajja) means: having reached, having obtained. Hearing this, the Licchavi king thought: “This Dhamma cannot be penetrated by flying up like a bird, nor can it be penetrated by going on one’s chest like an iguana. Surely, for one who is to penetrate this, there must be a preliminary practice. Let me first ask about it.”

entries.pali: 1004-5 . Aṭṭhame ñātike ti ekaṃ taḷākaṃ nissāya dvinnaṃ cūḷapitimahāpitiputtānaṃ dve gāmā, tesu ekasmiṃ gāmake. Giñjakāvasathe ti iṭṭhakāmaye āvasathe. Orambhāgiyāna nti heṭṭhābhāgiyānaṃ, kāmabhaveyeva paṭisandhiggāhāpakānanti attho. Oranti laddhanāmehi vā tīhi maggehi pahātabbānītipi orambhāgiyāni. Tattha kāmacchando byāpādoti imāni dve samāpattiyā vā avikkhambhitāni maggena vā asamucchinnāni nibbattivasena uddhaṃ bhāgaṃ rūpabhavaṃ arūpabhavaṃ vā gantuṃ na denti. Sakkāyadiṭṭhiādīni tīṇi tattha nibbattampi ānetvā puna idheva nibbattāpentīti sabbānipi orambhāgiyāneva. Anāvattidhammo ti paṭisandhivasena anāgamanasabhāvo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 第八，‘在亲族村’(Ñātike)是指：靠近一个池塘，有叔父与伯父之子的两个村庄；于此二村之一。‘在砖屋’(Giñjakāvasathe)即在砖造的住所里。‘下分结’(orambhāgiyāni)的意思是属于下界的，即能导致在欲界(kāmabhava)结生的诸结。或者，因其当为名为‘下’(ora)的三道所断，故名下分结。其中，欲贪(kāmacchanda)和瞋恚(byāpāda)这二者，若未被定(samāpatti)所镇伏，或未被道所断除，则不令[众生]得以往生上分，即色界(rūpabhava)或无色界(arūpabhava)。有身见(sakkāyadiṭṭhi)等三结，即使[众生]已生于彼处，亦将其带回，再令其生于此处，是故全部皆为下分结。‘不还法’(anāvattidhammo)即依结生而言，具有不再返回的自性。
entries.english: In the eighth sutta, regarding Ñātika: near a single reservoir, there were two villages belonging to the sons of a younger and an elder paternal uncle. Because these were the villages of two sets of kinsmen (ñāti), they received the name Ñātika. In one of those villages, Giñjakāvasatha means in a dwelling made of bricks. Orambhāgiyāni (lower fetters) means those belonging to the lower part; the meaning is that they cause one to take rebirth only in the sensual realm. Alternatively, they are called orambhāgiyāni because they are to be abandoned by the three paths which are named 'lower' (ora). Among these, sensual desire and ill will, if not suppressed by meditative attainments or eradicated by the path, do not allow one to proceed to a higher state—the form realm or the formless realm—by way of rebirth. The three fetters beginning with identity view, even for one who has arisen there, bring them back and cause them to be reborn right here. Thus, all five are indeed lower fetters. Anāvattidhamma (one not subject to return) means having the nature of not returning, by way of rebirth.

entries.pali: 33 . Khandhabījaṃ nāma paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ. Ihaṭṭhakanijjhānikavaseneva imasmiṃ ṭhāne kathitā ti sajjhānako ajjhattasaṃyojanasamucchede akatepi anāgāmisabhāgo anāvattidhammo idha gaṇanūpago na hoti, heṭṭhā upari ca saṃsaraṇako kāmabhavagato hīnajjhānako idha gaṇanūpagoti adhippāyo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 33. “蕴种”(Khandhabīja)即结生识。此处是仅依现世禅修者而说。因此，有禅那者，即便未断尽内结，若是有分于不还、属不还法者，此处亦不计入；而于下上轮回、生于欲有、得劣禅者，此处则计入，此为意趣。
entries.english: 33. 'Seed of the aggregates' is a name for rebirth-linking consciousness. Since this is stated here in terms of one who is an attainer of jhāna, one who possesses jhāna and is of a nature similar to a non-returner, one of irreversible nature, is not included in this count, even though the destruction of the internal fetters has not been accomplished. The intention is that one who wanders below and above, who has gone to the sense-sphere existence, who has inferior jhāna, is included in this count.

entries.pali: Heṭṭhā ti ‘‘amahaggatabhūmiya’’nti heṭṭhā sambandhanena. Heṭṭhābhāgassa hitāti heṭṭhābhāgiyā, tesaṃ. Tānīti orabbhāgiyasaṃyojanāni. Kāmāvacare nibbattatiyeva ajjhattaṃ saṃyojanattā. Tathā hesa dūratopi āvattidhammo evāti dassetuṃ gilabaḷisamacchādayo upamābhāvena vuttā. Opapātiko ti iminā gabbhavāsadukkhābhāvamāha. Tattha parinibbāyī ti iminā sesadukkhābhāvaṃ. Tattha parinibbānatā cassa kāmaloke khandhabījassa apunārohavasenevāti dassetuṃ ‘‘anāvattidhammo’’ ti vuttaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘下分’(heṭṭhā)是与‘非广大地’(amahaggatabhūmi)下方之关联。‘下分结’(heṭṭhābhāgiyā)即属于下分，指彼等（结）。‘彼等’指下分结(orambhāgiyasaṃyojanāni)。由于是内在之结缚，故必定会投生于欲界(kāmāvacara)。为表明即使彼人离得很远，仍有返回之法，故用吞钩之鱼等作譬喻。‘化生’(opapātiko)意指没有住胎之苦。‘于彼处般涅槃’(tattha parinibbāyī)意指没有剩余之苦。为表明于彼处般涅槃是因为欲界之蕴的种子不再生长的缘故，故说‘不还法’(anāvattidhammo)。
entries.english: Heṭṭhā (below) is connected with ‘in the non-exalted plane’ below. Heṭṭhābhāgiyā means ‘pertaining to the lower part’, belonging to them. Tāni (those) refers to the lower fetters. He is indeed reborn in the sense-sphere because of the internal fetters. Similarly, to show that he is by nature subject to turning back even from afar, the examples of the swallowed hook, the fish, and so on are given as similes. Opapātiko means ‘of spontaneous birth’; by this, the absence of the suffering of dwelling in a womb is indicated. Tattha parinibbāyī means ‘there attains final Nibbāna’; by this, the absence of remaining suffering is indicated. And to show that his attaining final Nibbāna there in the sense-world is just by way of the aggregate-seed not sprouting again, it is said, ‘not subject to returning’.

entries.pali: Opapātiko ti upapātikayoniko upapatane sādhukārī. Sesayonipaṭikkhepavacanametaṃ. Tena gabbhavāsadukkhābhāvamāha. Tattha parinibbāyī ti iminā sesadukkhābhāvaṃ. Tattha parinibbāyitā cassa kāmaloke khandhabījassa apunāgamanavasenevāti dassetuṃ ‘‘anāvattidhammo’’ ti vuttaṃ. Upariyevā ti brahmalokeyeva. Anāvattidhammo ti tato brahmalokā punappunaṃ paṭisandhivasena na āvattanadhammo. Tenāha ‘‘yonigativasena anāgamanadhammo’’ ti.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘化生者’(opapātika)，即化生类有情，能顺利化生。此为排斥其余生类之语，以此说明无住胎之苦。其中，以‘于彼处般涅槃’(tattha parinibbāyī)说明其余诸苦亦无。为示其于彼处般涅槃，且因欲界蕴种不再来之故，而说‘不还法’(anāvattidhamma)。‘唯上’(upariyeva)即唯于梵天界。‘不还法’者，谓不复以结生(paṭisandhi)从彼梵天界返回之法。故说‘就趣之生类而言，是不来之法’。
entries.english: 'Spontaneously born' (opapātika) means one of spontaneous origin, one who is born spontaneously. This is a statement that excludes the other kinds of birth. By this, he indicates the absence of the suffering of dwelling in a womb. By 'there he attains final Nibbāna' (parinibbāyī), he indicates the absence of remaining suffering. And to show that his attaining final Nibbāna there is precisely by way of the non-return of the seed of the aggregates to the sense-sphere world, it is said, 'of a nature not to return' (anāvattidhammo). 'Only above' means only in the Brahma world. 'Of a nature not to return' means he is not of a nature to return from that Brahma world again and again by way of rebirth-linking. Therefore he said, 'of a nature not to come again by way of birth-origin and destination.'

entries.pali: Sakadāgāmiphalañca yo sakadāgāmiphale ṭhito vipassanaṃ bhāvento kāmarāgabyāpāde sānusaye anavasesaṃ pajahati, kāmarāgabyāpādesu anavasesaṃ pahīnesu pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni bhavanti sakkāyadiṭṭhi sīlabbataparāmāso vicikicchā kāmacchando byāpādo ca, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānā pahānāya (pī. ka.) ariyasāvako hoti anāgāmī tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā, ayaṃ vītarāgabhūmi.
entries.chinese_simplified: 住一来果者，修习观时，连同随眠无余舍断欲贪、瞋恚。欲贪、瞋恚无余断尽时，五下分结即被断除，即：身见、戒禁取、疑、欲贪与瞋恚。因断此五下分结，圣弟子成不还者，于彼处般涅槃，不复还来此世间，此为离贪地。
entries.english: And a once-returner, established in the fruit of the once-returner, by developing insight, abandons sensual desire and ill will together with their underlying tendencies without remainder. When sensual desire and ill will have been abandoned without remainder, the five lower fetters are abandoned: identity view, clinging to rules and observances, doubt, sensual desire, and ill will. With the abandonment of these five lower fetters, the noble disciple becomes a non-returner, one who attains final Nibbāna there, not of a nature to return from that world. This is the ground free from lust.

entries.pali: 33 . Sajjhānako aparihīnajjhāno kālakato brahmalokūpago hutvā vaṭṭajjhāsayo ce, uparūpari nibbattitvā nibbāyatīti āha ‘‘anāgāmisabhāgo’’ ti. Yato so jhānānāgāmīti vuccati. Tenāha ‘‘anāvattidhammo’’ ti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 33. 有禅定而不退失者，命终生于梵天界后，若有轮回之倾向，则辗转上生而般涅槃，故说为“不还者之分”。因此，他被称为禅那不还者。是故说为“不还法”。
entries.english: 33. He says, ‘he has a share in non-returning,’ meaning: if one with jhāna, who has not fallen away from jhāna, having passed away and gone to the brahma-world, has an inclination for the round, he is reborn higher and higher and attains Nibbāna. Since he is called a ‘jhāna non-returner,’ he says, ‘one whose nature is not to return.’

path: 雷迪西亚多著作集 Leḍī-Sayāḍo-Gantha-Saṅgaho
entries.pali: Idhānanda bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ pathamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So yadeva tattha hoti rūpagataṃ vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ, te dhamme aniccato dukkhato anattato samanupassati. So tattha ṭhito āsavānaṃ khayaṃ pāpuṇāti. No ce āsavānaṃ khayaṃ pāpuṇāti. Teneva dhammarāgena tāya dhammanandiyā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā upapātiko hoti. Tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokāti.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘于此，阿难，有比丘离诸欲，离诸不善法，有寻有伺，离生喜乐，成就并安住于初禅。彼于彼处，凡有属于色、受、想、行、识之法，皆随观为无常、苦、无我。彼安住于此，证得诸漏灭尽。若未证得诸漏灭尽，则因于法之贪，于法之喜，五下分结断尽，成为化生者，于彼处般涅槃，不复从此世间退转。’
entries.english: Here, Ānanda, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. He regards whatever phenomena there that are connected with form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self. Standing there, he attains the destruction of the taints. If he does not attain the destruction of the taints, then through that very delight in the Dhamma, that joy in the Dhamma, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, he is one who arises spontaneously. There he attains final Nibbāna, not liable to return from that world.
